subject: ela
intro: This worksheet covers the whole Key Ideas and Details cluster for grade 4 literature: referring to explicit details and drawing inferences with evidence (4.RL.A.1), determining a theme and summarizing (4.RL.A.2), and describing a character, setting, or event in depth using specific details (4.RL.A.3). Items are grouped by standard and get harder toward the end of each group.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Sofia laid out her paints, clipped a blank sheet to her easel, and squinted at the mountains in the distance before dipping her brush.

What is Sofia about to do? Name the detail that tells you.
items.answer: Sofia is about to paint a picture of the mountains. She lays out her paints, clips paper to her easel, and studies the mountains before dipping her brush.

steps: List the clues: paints, easel, blank sheet, studying the mountains.
These are the steps an artist takes before painting.
So she is about to paint the mountains.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Aiden checked the clock for the fifth time, tapped his foot, and kept glancing at the door. Every time a car passed the window, he sat up straight.

What can you infer about Aiden? Use a detail.
items.answer: You can infer Aiden is waiting for someone and is impatient or excited. He keeps checking the clock, glancing at the door, and sitting up "every time a car passed," which shows he is expecting someone to arrive.

steps: Explicit details: checking the clock, tapping his foot, watching the door and cars.
Add what you know: these are signs of waiting eagerly.
So Aiden is impatiently waiting for someone.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The teacher asked who had left the classroom window open in the rain. Everyone looked at Sam, whose sleeve was soaked and who was quietly mopping the sill with paper towels.

Who most likely left the window open, and which details tell you?
items.answer: Sam most likely left the window open. His "sleeve was soaked" and he was "quietly mopping the sill with paper towels," which suggests he is cleaning up his own mistake.

steps: The clues are Sam's soaked sleeve and his quiet mopping.
Someone cleaning up the wet sill is likely the one responsible.
So Sam most likely left it open.

items.prompt:
Read the poem.

Her boots stand empty by the door,
Her coat hangs still upon its hook.
The kettle waits, the cup is dry,
And no one turns the page of her book.

What can you infer about the person the poem describes? Point to a detail.
items.answer: You can infer the person is away or gone, because her things are untouched. Her boots "stand empty," her coat hangs "still," the cup is "dry," and "no one turns the page of her book," all showing she is not there.

steps: The boots, coat, cup, and book are all still and unused.
Add what you know: untouched belongings mean the owner is absent.
So the person is away or gone.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Every afternoon, Grandpa set two cups of tea on the porch table, though his old friend Sal had moved away years ago. He would sip his own, leave the second cup untouched, and watch the sunset alone. "Habits," he said softly, "are hard to break."

What can you infer about how Grandpa feels about his old friend? Support your inference with details.
items.answer: You can infer Grandpa still misses his old friend Sal deeply. He sets out "two cups of tea" even though Sal "moved away years ago," leaves the second cup untouched, and says "habits are hard to break," showing he holds on to the memory of their friendship.

steps: Grandpa still pours a second cup for a friend who is gone.
He leaves it untouched and watches the sunset alone.
This shows he misses Sal and keeps the habit out of love.

items.prompt:
Read the fable.

A boy cried "Wolf!" as a joke, and the whole village ran to help, only to find him laughing. He did it again the next day. But when a real wolf came and the boy cried out, no one believed him, and no one came.

What is the theme of this fable?
items.answer: The theme is that if you lie again and again, people will stop believing you, even when you tell the truth. The boy's false alarms mean no one comes when the real wolf appears.

steps: The boy lies twice for fun.
When he tells the truth, no one believes him.
The lesson is that repeated lies destroy trust.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Tara wanted the newest phone like her friends had. Her parents said she could earn it by saving her allowance. It took eight long months, but when she finally bought it with her own money, she felt a pride she had never felt before.

What is the theme of this story, and how does the ending show it?
items.answer: The theme is that earning something through your own effort makes it more meaningful. After saving for eight months, Tara feels "a pride she had never felt before" because she bought the phone with her own money.

steps: Tara works and saves for eight months to earn the phone.
She feels a special pride when she buys it herself.
The lesson is that things earned feel more rewarding.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

When a new girl who spoke little English joined the class, some kids laughed at her accent. Lucia sat with her at lunch, learned a few words in the girl's language, and taught her a few in return. By spring the two were best friends, and no one laughed anymore.

Write a one-sentence summary, then state the theme.
items.answer: Summary: When a new girl who speaks little English is teased, Lucia befriends her by sharing words in each other's languages until they become best friends and the teasing stops. Theme: Kindness and trying to understand others can build friendship and end cruelty.

steps: Summary: Lucia befriends the teased new girl by sharing languages.
They become best friends and the teasing ends.
Theme: kindness and understanding build friendship and stop cruelty.

items.prompt:
Read the fable.

The wind and the sun argued over who was stronger. They agreed the winner would make a traveler remove his coat. The wind blew hard and cold, but the man only clutched his coat tighter. Then the sun shone warm and gentle, and soon the man took the coat off himself.

What is the theme of this fable, and how do the wind's and sun's actions show it?
items.answer: The theme is that gentleness and warmth can succeed where force fails. The wind's harsh blowing makes the man clutch his coat tighter, but the sun's gentle warmth makes him remove it willingly.

steps: The wind uses force but fails.
The sun uses warmth and gentleness and succeeds.
The lesson is that kindness works better than force.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The king ordered the finest builders to raise the tallest tower in the world. They stacked the stones so high, so fast, that they skipped checking the foundation. On the day it was finished, the great tower leaned, cracked, and crumbled to dust. A humble mason who had built a small, sturdy well nearby only shook his head and kept drawing his water.

Write a short summary of the story, then explain its theme.
items.answer: Summary: The king's builders race to raise the tallest tower but skip the foundation, so it crumbles, while a humble mason's small, sturdy well still stands. Theme: A strong, careful foundation matters more than rushing to be the biggest or fastest, so patient, solid work lasts longer than showy ambition.

steps: Summary: the rushed tower with no foundation collapses; the careful well survives.
The contrast points to the lesson.
Theme: careful, solid work outlasts rushed, showy ambition.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

When the ball rolled into the busy street, the little boy started to chase it. Fourth-grader Dev grabbed his backpack strap, pulled him back onto the sidewalk, and said firmly, "Cars first, ball later."

Describe Dev using a detail from the story.
items.answer: Dev is alert and protective. He grabs the little boy's backpack strap to pull him back from the street and says, "Cars first, ball later," keeping the boy safe.

steps: Name a trait: Dev is alert and protective.
Find the action: he pulls the boy back and warns him about cars.
Use that as proof.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The hospital waiting room was quiet and pale green, with rows of stiff chairs and an old clock ticking loudly on the wall. Magazines lay in neat, untouched stacks, and the only sound was the squeak of a nurse's shoes on the shiny floor.

Describe the setting and how it might make someone feel. Use two details.
items.answer: The setting is a quiet, pale green hospital waiting room that feels tense and lonely. The "rows of stiff chairs" and the "old clock ticking loudly" make the wait feel slow and anxious.

steps: Name the place: a hospital waiting room.
Pick details: stiff chairs, loud ticking clock, untouched magazines.
These details make it feel tense and lonely.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

At first, Priya wanted to win the art contest so badly that she hid the good brushes so no one else could use them. But when she saw a classmate struggling with a broken brush, something in her shifted. She quietly pulled out a spare and handed it over. "Here," she said. "Your painting deserves a fair chance."

Describe how Priya changes, using details from the beginning and end.
items.answer: Priya changes from selfish to generous. At first she "hid the good brushes" so no one else could win, but after seeing a classmate struggle she hands over a spare brush and says, "Your painting deserves a fair chance," showing she chooses fairness over winning.

steps: Beginning: Priya hides brushes to win.
End: she gives a struggling classmate a spare brush.
The change is from selfish to generous and fair.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The blizzard trapped the family inside for three days. The power went out, the windows frosted over, and the wind howled without stopping. But inside, Dad lit candles, Mom told stories from her childhood, and the kids built a fort of blankets. By the third night, they almost hoped the snow would last a little longer.

Describe how the harsh setting and the family's actions work together to shape the mood.
items.answer: The harsh setting of the blizzard, with no power, frosted windows, and howling wind, could feel scary, but the family's actions change the mood. Dad lighting candles, Mom telling stories, and the kids building a blanket fort turn the cold, trapped days into a cozy, happy time, so much that they "almost hoped the snow would last a little longer."

steps: Setting: a dark, cold, howling blizzard traps the family.
Their actions: candles, stories, and a blanket fort.
Together they turn a scary setting into a warm, cozy mood.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Everyone knew Coach Ramos as the strictest coach in the league, quick to make players run extra laps for a missed pass. So the team was stunned when, after they lost the championship, he gathered them close and said quietly, "I have never been prouder of a team." He pointed to how they had helped an injured player off the field and cheered for a rival's good play. "Trophies fade," he said. "The way you treat people does not."

Describe Coach Ramos in depth, using specific words and actions from the text.
items.answer: Coach Ramos is strict but deeply caring, and he values character over winning. He is "quick to make players run extra laps," showing his strictness, but after the loss he gathers the team and says, "I have never been prouder of a team," praising how they helped an injured player and cheered a rival. His words "Trophies fade. The way you treat people does not" reveal that he cares most about how his players treat others.

steps: Name traits: strict but caring, values character over winning.
Strict: he makes players run extra laps.
Caring: after losing he praises their kindness and says how they treat people matters most.
